reference.source: Dhingra Diseases of ENT 8th Edition (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
clinicalPearls: Ludwig angina is bilateral, dental, airway first
Lemierre: Fusobacterium jugular thrombophlebitis after pharyngitis
reference.pathophysiology: Fascial planes guide pus predictably while venous drainage seeds internal jugular thrombophlebitis; floor of mouth swelling displaces tongue posteriorly against epiglottis in closed oral cavity.
additionalDifferentials: Ludwig cellulitis versus abscess (drainage still often needed)
Retropharyngeal abscess versus epiglottitis in child (neck stiffness, imaging)
Lemierre versus simple tonsillitis by sepsis and neck pain timing
additionalInvestigations: Contrast CT neck and chest when airway stable
Blood cultures before antibiotics when safe
